items.readable_text:
Content:
When we want to calculate the square of a binomial, like

Content:
[MATH: (a+b)^2,]

Content:
there's a formula that we can use instead of working out the product [MATH: (a+b)(a+b)] manually. The formula is

Content:
[MATH: (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2.]

Content:
It might be helpful to remember this as "the square of the first term, plus the square of the second term, plus twice the product."

Content:
Suppose we need to calculate the square [MATH: (x+3)^2.] In this case, we have [MATH: a= x] and [MATH: b=3.] We substitute into the formula and simplify:

Content:
[MATH: (x + 3)^{2}|=; (x)^{2} + 2(x)(3) + (3)^{2}|=; x^{2} + 6x + 9]

Content:
We can check that the formula gives the correct result by working out the multiplication manually:

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
(x + 3)^2 &= \[3pt]
(x + 3)(x + 3) &= \[3pt]
x(x + 3) + 3(x + 3) &= \[3pt]
x^2 + 3x + 3x + 9 &= \[3pt]
x^2 + 6x + 9 &\, {\color{green}{\checkmark}}
}]

Content:
So we get the same result! But by using the formula, we save a lot of time and effort.

Content:
So far, we've been using the formula for the square of a binomial involving addition:
[MATH: (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2]
There is also a similar formula that we can use to compute the square of a binomial involving subtraction. The formula is
[MATH: (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2.]

Content:
For example, to compute the square [MATH: (x-3)^2,] we can substitute [MATH: a=x] and [MATH: b=3] into the formula and simplify:

Content:
[MATH: (x − 3)^{2}|=; (x)^{2} − 2(x)(3) + (3)^{2}|=; x^{2} − 6x + 9]

Content:
We can check that the formula gives the correct result by working out the multiplication manually:

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
(x - 3)^2 &= \
(x - 3)(x - 3) &= \
x(x - 3) - 3(x - 3) &= \
x^2 - 3x - 3x + 9 &= \
x^2 - 6x + 9 &\, {\color{green}{\checkmark}}
}]

Content:
Again, we get the same result.

Content:

Content:
It might be helpful to remember this as "the square of the first term, plus the square of the second term, plus twice the product."

Content:

}]
